data: この 漢字[かんじ]の 書[か]き方[かた]は、 覚[おぼ]えても 覚[おぼ]えなくても いいです。
It doesn't matter whether or not you memorize the way to write this kanji.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-te も V-nai なくても "Whether V or not"
便利[べんり]さと いう 点[てん]から 考[かんが]えると、 この アパートが 一番[いちばん]だ。
From a convenience standpoint, this apartment is the best.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N という点から考えると "to view from the standpoint of ~; from the perspective of ~" used to indicate someone's view from the standpoint of X. Examples of X include business, environment, education, etc.
多[おお]くの 人々[ひとびと]が 早[はや]く 世界[せかい]が 平和[へいわ]になる ように願[ねが]っている。
Many people hope that we'll have a peaceful world soon.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S-plain.nonpast ように（と）願う Means: hope that ~ And is used to express the speaker's hope or desire that what is stated in the sentence will become a reality.
友達[ともだち]が 手伝[てつだ]ってくれた おかげで、 仕事[しごと]が 早[はや]く終[お]わった。
Thanks to my friend helping me out, work ended early.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-plain おかげ "because; due to" Both おかげ and せい are dependent nouns indicating cause. The former is used when the cause brings about a desirable result, and the latter when the cause brings about an unwanted result.
海外[かいがい] 旅行[りょこう]に 行[い]く 前[まえ]に パスポートを 取[と]る 必要[ひつよう]が あります。
Before traveling overseas it is necessary to get a passport.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This phrase is used to indicate the necessity of doing something. は is common with a negative ending. --- 英訳 [English translation]: a. V必要がある = It is necessary to V; must V; have to V. b. V必要はない = It is not necessary to V; there is no need to V; don't have to V. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-past 必要{がある/はない}
今年[ことし]の 夏[なつ]は 寒[さむ]い 日[ひ]が 続[つづ]いて、 全然[ぜんぜん] 夏[なつ]らしく ありません。
Summer this year has been cold day after day; it doesn't feel summery at all.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
〜らしくない／らしくありません Means: not much like, not typical of ~; not typical~; not X-like.
人生[じんせい]は 考[かんが]え方[かた] 次第[しだい]で、 楽[たの]しくも なれば、 苦[くる]しくも なる。
Your life can be enjoyable or painful depending on how you view things.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

A-stem くも V-cond ば, 〜も "some do ~ and others do ~; do ~ and ~ among other things; sometimes ~ and sometimes ~; there are times when ~ and times when ~; ~ and also ~; ~ and ~ as well" This structure is used to present actions or states (usually 2) as examples of possible or past actions/states. In many cases the actions/states are contrastive ones.
漢字[かんじ]が 苦手[にがて]だと 言[い]っても、 全然[ぜんぜん] 書[か]けない わけでは ない。
Although I say that kanji is my weak point, that doesn't mean I can't write them at all.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{V/A} (という）わけではない。 Means: It's not that~; It doesn't mean that used to deny a statement.
数学[すうがく]と 同[おな]じで、 物理[ぶつり]も 公式[こうしき]を 勉強[べんきょう] しなくては ならない。
You have to study formulas when you study physics, just like when you study math.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The comparison phrases と同じで and と違って mean "just like ~" and "unlike ~", respectively. Note that the particle と is used when X and Y are in a reciprocal relationship --- 英訳 [English translation]: N と同じで = just like N N と違って = unlike N; different from N --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N と{同じ/違って}
この 教科[きょうか]書[しょ]は、 会話[かいわ]も 練習[れんしゅう] できるし、 文化[ぶんか]も 学[まな]べます。
With this textbook you can practice conversation and study culture among other things.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1も V-plain し、N2も V Means: do ~ and ~ among other things; sometimes ~ and sometimes ~; ~ and also ~; ~ and ~ as well; other meanings exist: pg 142 in とびら
この 教科[きょうか]書[しょ]は、 会話[かいわ]も 練習[れんしゅう] できれば、 文化[ぶんか]も 学[まな]べます。
With this textbook you can practice conversation and study culture among other things.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1も V-conditional, N2 も V。 Means: some do ~ and others do ~; do ~ and ~ among other things; sometimes ~ and sometimes ~; there are times when ~ and times when ~; ~ and also ~; ~ and ~ as well. This sentence structure is used to present some members in a group, things in a category, actions someone takes, characteristics of something/someone, etc. among others. Although the form of the verb here is conditional, the meaning is NOT conditional in its usage.
この アパート、 良[よ]さ そうだけど、 ちょっと 高[たか]すぎるかな。
This apartment seems nice, but I wonder if it's a bit too expensive.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 〜かなあ is a sentence final particle which indicates that the sentence is a self-addressed question or a question addressed to the speaker's in-group member(s). It is used only in casual language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: I wonder ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜かな(あ)
これらの 問題[もんだい]に ついて もっと 話[はな]し合[あ]ってみる 必要[ひつよう]が ある。
We need to try discussing these problems more.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

Demonstrative pronounら "these; those; they; -s; and others" [plural dem. pronouns can be used in polite speech] The plural marker ら is often used with demonstrative pronouns and certain personal pronouns. plural personal pronouns are not used in polite speech.
田中[たなか]さん、 ５[ご]時[じ]に 来[く]るって 言[い]ってたけど、 未[いま]だ 来[こ]ないね。
Mr. Tanaka said he'd come at 5:00, but he still hasn't come, has he?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: って is the informal colloquial form of the quotative marker と. って commonly occurs with verbs like 言う, 聞く, 書く and 呼ぶ. --- 英訳 [English translation]: (tell, hear, say, etc.) that ~ Noun1っていうNoun2 = Noun2 called Noun1 --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Sって{言う/聞く/書く} b. Nって{言う/聞く/呼ぶ} c. N1っていうN2
漢字[かんじ]を 覚[おぼ]えるには フラッシュ カードを 作[つく]るのが 一番[いちばん]です。
Making flash cards is the best way to memorize kanji.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past.aff には "to; in order to; for; for the purpose of; when" には indicates purpose in general statements (often stating the speaker's judgement about an action in terms of its effectiveness, convenience, necessity, etc.). には can also mean "when" (=時には). Verbs or nouns can precede には. Note that when ために is used, the predicate in the main clause describes an action. Such that: Xには Y, where Y is a judgment and never an action XためにY, where Y is an action and never a judgement. AND, XためにはY, where Y is a judgment, never an action
YouTubeは 面白[おもしろ]い。だが、 問題[もんだい]の ある 動画[どうが]も 多[おお]い。
YouTube is interesting, but there are also a lot of problematic video clips.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1. だが、S2. "but; however" だが is a disjunctive conjunction. S1 and S2 present contrastive statements or opposing ideas. Note: でも、けれど、けど are colloquial けれども、しかしながら、だが、and が are primarily used in written language. しかし can be used in both written and spoken language.
今度[こんど] 住[す]む アパートは、 この 部屋[へや]と 同[おな]じぐらいの 広[ひろ]さです。
The apartment I'm going to live in next is about the same size as this room.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The particle ぐらい/くらい "approximately" often occurs with 同じ to mean "about the same." --- 英訳 [English translation]: about as ~ as; about the same ~ as ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N と同じ{ぐらい/くらい} b. N1 と同じ{ぐらい/くらい}の N2
母[はは]の 料理[りょうり]が いかに おいしいかは、 言葉[ことば]では 説明[せつめい] できない。
There are no words to describe just how delicious my mother's cooking is.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
いかに〜か "how; how much; in what way" This structure occurs as an embedded interrogative sentence, where いかに means "how (much)" or "in what way". This structure is commonly used in written language.
両親[りょうしん]は 私[わたし]に、 いつも 早[はや]く 家[いえ]に 帰[かえ]ってくる ように 言[い]います。
My parents always tell me to come home early.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように頼む/言う is used to quote a request or command indirectly. In an affirmative request ように頼む is often used with てくれる, as in 来てくれるように頼む. (cf. negative request: ~ないように頼む --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~(てくれる)ように頼む = to ask someone to V ~ように言う = to tell someone to V --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. V-non-plast.plain ように頼む/言う b. V-te くれるように頼む c. V-nai ないように頼む/言う
明日[あした]の 試験[しけん]では、 言[い]うまでも なく、 文法[ぶんぽう]の 問題[もんだい]が 出[で]ます。
Needless to say, there will be grammar questions on tomorrow's test.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

（Xは）言うまでもなく、S。 "needless to say; it goes without saying that ~; it is obvious that ~; not to mention ~; let alone ~" This phrase is used when the speaker mentions something obvious or something assumed to be known to the hearer. It is commonly used in written language.
ハンサムな せいで、 うそを 信[しん]じて、 ばかな ことを しました。
Because he was handsome, I believed his lies and did foolish things.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ANa {な/じゃない／だった／じゃなかった} せい／おかげ "because; due to" Both おかげ and せい are dependent nouns indicating cause. The former is used when the cause brings about a desirable result, and the latter when the cause brings about an unwanted result. Both おかげ and せい are dependent nouns indicating cause. The former is used when the cause brings about a desirable result, and the latter when the cause brings about an unwanted result.
お酒[さけ]さえ 飲[の]まなければ、 何[なに]を 飲[の]んでも 食[た]べても いいですよ。
You can drink and eat whatever you want as long as you don't drink alcohol.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Noun さえ with a verb conditional form is used when the condition presented in the clause is the only condition to make the statement in the main clause true. さえ replaces が and を in this structure; however, when other particles occur with さえ here, they do not drop. --- 英訳 [English translation]: If~ only ~; If~ just ~; as long as; --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N( = clause X) さえ V-cond (= clause Y)
宿題[しゅくだい]を しようと したが、 友達[ともだち]が 来[き]たから、 するのを やめた。
I was going to do my homework, but friends came over so I stopped doing it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-volとした, the past form of V-volとする(to try to do ~), is used in situations when someone had made an attempt to do something but failed, where someone was going to do something but didn't, or where something happened when someone was going to do something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-volとした{が／けれど} = tried to ~, but; was going to ~, but V-volとしたら = when ~ was going to ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-volとした{が／けれど}: 行こうとした{が／けれど／ら}; 食べようとした{が／けれど／ら}
調[しら]べなきゃならない ことが あるので、 図書[としょ]館[かん]に 行[い]って来[く]る。
I have things I have to research so I'm going to the library.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: These patterns express the idea of obligation. Although the two patterns are interchangeable, there is a subtle difference between ならない and いけない. That is, ならない is commonly used when the speaker states his/her sense of obligation while いけない is commonly used when the sense of obligation is directed towards the hearer (i.e. when the speaker wants to impose a certain obligation on the hearer). The following contracted forms are used in casual conversation: なきゃならない -> なきゃなんない なくちゃならない -> なくちゃんなんない --- 英訳 [English translation]: have to; must; should --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜なければ{いけない/ならない} 〜なくては{いけない/ならない}
私[わたし]は 来週[らいしゅう]、 学校[がっこう]の 代表[だいひょう]と して スピーチ コンテストに 出[で]ます。
Next week, I'm participating in a speech contest as the representative from my school.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: として is used to indicate the role, capacity, or occupation of someone or the function or characteristics of something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: as; in the capacity of --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nとして1
人々[ひとびと]の 生活[せいかつ]の 変化[へんか]に 合[あ]わせて、 家[いえ]の 形[かたち]も 変[か]わってきました。
Housing styles have also changed to match the change in people's lifestyles.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N に会わせて "making ~ suitable for N; according to N" The literal meaning this grammar is "fitting/matching/adjusting something to N" and is often used to mean "making something suitable for N" or "according to N"
みんなが 同時[どうじ]に 話[はな]さないで、 一人[ひとり]ずつ 順番[じゅんばん]に 話[はな]して下[くだ]さい。
Please don't all talk at once - take turns and speak one at a time.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{Number +(counter)} +ずつ "per/a; at a time; each; (little) by (little)" The number/amount X+ずつ indicates that someone does something (or something happens) with X as the unit.
週末[しゅうまつ]は、 勉強[べんきょう] 以外[いがい]に、 テニスを したり 映画[えいが]を 見[み]たり します。
Besides studying, I do things like play tennis and watch movies on the weekend.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{N/DemP} 以外に "Besides N/DemP" X以外に means "besides X" and に is sometimes omitted.
大学[だいがく]に 入[はい]って 以来[いらい]、 高校[こうこう] 時代[じだい]の 友達[ともだち]に 一度[いちど]も 会[あ]っていない。
I haven't seen my high school friends even once since I started college.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-te 以来 "since" It is used with V-te or VN referring to an action in the past, or with N indicating a specific time in the past.
インスタント ラーメンは、 たった 3[さん]分[ぷん]で できるので 便利[べんり]です。
Instant ramen takes just three minutes to make, so it's really convenient.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
たった（の）Number (+counter) "only" This is used to emphasize the small amount or number of something.
その アルバイトは あまり 大変[たいへん]じゃないし、 それに 給料[きゅうりょう]も いい。
That part-time job isn't very difficult, and moreover, the salary is good.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: それに is used to add an item or make an addition statement. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in addition; moreover; furthermore; what's more; on top of that; and --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N1 {、/と / に} N2, それに N3 b. S1。それに、S2。 c. S1 し、それに、S2。
ここから ペンギンが 水[みず]の 中[なか]で 泳[およ]いでいる ところが 見[み]られます。
You can see the penguins swimming underwater from here.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V−teいるところ Means: (when)~ is V-ing; (while)~is V-ing; (when)~ is in the midst of V-ing ところ indicates a point in time just before, during, or just after an event, the time indicated depends on the preceding verb tense.
分[わ]からない ときは、 もう 一度[いちど]、 読[よ]み直[なお]してみるといいですよ。
When you don't understand something, it helps to try reading it one more time.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-masu 直す "again, re-V" 直す, when attached to the masu-stems of verbs, creates compound verbs with the meaning "again; re-."
私[わたし]は よく 両親[りょうしん]に 「弟[おとうと]を いじめては いけません」と 言[い]われます。
I'm often told by my parents, "You mustn't tease your little brother."
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように頼む/言う is used to quote a request or command indirectly. In an affirmative request ように頼む is often used with てくれる, as in 来てくれるように頼む. (cf. negative request: ~ないように頼む --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~(てくれる)ように頼む = to ask someone to V ~ように言う = to tell someone to V --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. V-non-plast.plain ように頼む/言う b. V-te くれるように頼む c. V-nai ないように頼む/言う
体[からだ]に いいから、 野菜[やさい]や 果物[くだもの]を たくさん 食[た]べる ようにしている。
Since they're good for you, I'm making an effort to eat lots of vegetables and fruit.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.non-pastようにする: indicates one's conscious effort to do something for some purpose. Here one makes an effort at every opportunity to do something to the degree that he or she can, but sometimes fails. Thus ようにする is often used for habitual actions. Note that this phrase differs from Vことにする, which indicates one's decision to do something and the action can be either a single or habitual one. --- 英訳 [English translation]: make an effort to~; make an effort so that~; try (one's best) to do ~; try one's best so that~. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-pastようにする: {食べる/食べない}ようにする
なるべく 辞書[じしょ]を 使[つか]わないで、 この 記事[きじ]を 読[よ]んでみてください。
Try to read this article using your dictionary as little as possible.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: なるべく with or without an adverb modifies the following verb phrase and adds the meaning "as (much) as possible." When there is no specific adverb after なるべく, it is usually interpreted as "as much as~" or "as often as~." --- 英訳 [English translation]: as much/often as possible; as ~ as possible --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ なるべく
人[ひと]に 何[なに]か してもらったら、 少[すく]なくとも お礼[れい]は 言[い]った 方[ほう]が いい。
If someone does something for you, at the very least, you should thank him for it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
少なくとも N (は） 少なくとも means "at least." It can be used with a noun or number. When used with a noun, は often follows the noun (or the particle after the noun), indicating that the noun is under focus.
海外[かいがい] 旅行[りょこう]には、 この スーツケースを 持[も]って行[い]くと 便利[べんり]ですよ。
For traveling overseas, it's useful to take this suitcase with you.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N (of a VN, or direct object of する) には "to; in order to; for; for the purpose of; when" には indicates purpose in general statements (often stating the speaker's judgement about an action in terms of its effectiveness, convenience, necessity, etc.). には can also mean "when" (=時には). Verbs or nouns can precede には. Note that when ために is used, the predicate in the main clause describes an action. Such that: Xには Y, where Y is a judgment and never an action XためにY, where Y is an action and never a judgement. AND, XためにはY, where Y is a judgment, never an action
残念[ざんねん]な ことに、 私[わたし]達[たち]の チームは 最後[さいご]の 試合[しあい]で 負[ま]けてしまった。
Unfortunately, our team lost in the last match.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ANa なことに “It is~ that~; I am/We are ~ that ~; To my ~" ことに is used to express the speaker's feeling or subjective judgment about what is said in the main clause. ことに can only be used with a limited set of words.
日本[にほん]の 有名[ゆうめい]な 小説[しょうせつ]が ハリウッドで 映画[えいが]化[か] される ことに なった。
It's been decided that a famous Japanese novel will be adapted for the screen in Hollywood.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The suffix 化[か] is affixed to nouns and no-adjectives and adds the meaning of "-ization," as in "mechanization" and "digitization." --- 英訳 [English translation]: ～化する = ize; make; become; change to ～化する = ization; making ~; becoming ~; changing to ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N + 化: 日本化; 専門化; 機械化 (mechanization); カタカナ化 b. NO-Adj + 化: 最適化 (optimization)
今[こん]学期[がっき]は 日本[にほん]語[ご]や アジアの 歴史[れきし]などの クラスを 取[と]っています。
This semester I am taking classes such as Japanese and Asian history.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: など indicates that the given list is not exhaustive. When more than one item is listed, や is commonly used to connect the item. --- 英訳 [English translation]: N1やN2など = N1, N2 and others. N1やN2などのN3 = N3 such as N1 and N2; N3 like N1 and N2. N1やN2など、N3 = N3 such as N1 and N2; N3 like N1 and N2. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N1やN2など({は / も / が / を / に / の / etc.)} (N1 and N2 can be words or phrases).
私[わたし]の 国[くに]では 日本[にほん]に 旅行[りょこう]に 行[い]く 時[とき]、 旅行[りょこう] ビザを 取[と]る 必要[ひつよう]は ない。
As for my country, when traveling to Japan it is not necessary to get a travel Visa.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This phrase is used to indicate the necessity of doing something. は is common with a negative ending. --- 英訳 [English translation]: a. V必要がある = It is necessary to V; must V; have to V. b. V必要はない = It is not necessary to V; there is no need to V; don't have to V. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-past 必要{がある/はない}
お金持[かねも]ちに なる ことは、 幸[しあわ]せになれると いう ことなのだろうか。
I wonder if becoming rich means you can become happy.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to indicate what X is or what X means. なのだ makes the statement more emphatic. To make this expression more formal, use である in place of だ. --- 英訳 [English translation]: X is Y; X means that Y --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ XはY(という)ことなの{である/だ} : 日本人のことなのである。
最近[さいきん]では、 歩[ある]くだけでなく、 サッカーを する ロボットまで ある。
Recently, there are even robots that not only walk but also play soccer.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N まで（も） "even; to even" までも is used to present something which is considered to be beyond one's expectation or imagination.
昔[むかし]、 昔[むかし]、 ある 所[ところ]に、 おじいさんと おばあさんが 住[す]んでいました。
Once upon a time, in a far away land, there lived an old man and an old woman.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: あるN is used when the speaker has a specific X in mind but does not want/need to be specific. ある日 refers to a specific day, ある有名人 refers to (a) specific famous person/people and ある所 refers to an imaginary place in a folk tale. --- 英訳 [English translation]: a; a certain; some; some (one/thing) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ あるN: ある人; ある町; ある年
この アパートは できたばかりなので、 何[なに]から 何[なに]まで 全部[ぜんぶ] 新[あたら]しい。
They just finished building this apartment, so everything in it is brand new.

Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{N/ANa/ANo} {である／であった／ではない／ではなかった} N である is the formal plain form of だ and can be affixed to nouns and -な／-の adjectives. である is used in formal writing. In very formal speech the polite form であります／ではありません may be used. である can occur before nouns in relative clauses while だ cannot.
この 料理[りょうり]は まずい わけでは ないけど、 油[あぶら]が 多[おお]いから、 あまり 食[た]べられない。
It's not that this dish is yucky, but there's a lot of oil so I can't eat much.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{V/A} (という）わけではない。 Means: It's not that~; It doesn't mean that used to deny a statement.
次[つぎ]の 電車[でんしゃ]が すぐ 来[く]るから、 急[いそ]ぐ ことは ありません。 ゆっくり 行[い]きましょう。
The next train will come soon, so we don't need to rush. Let's take our time.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-plain.non-past すること（は）ない "don't have to ~; don't need to ~; It's not necessary to ~; There is no need to ~" In casual conversation the は may drop.
この ゲーム 機[き]は、 安[やす]くて 使[つか]いやすいと いう 理由[りゆう]で、 よく 売[う]れている そうだ。
I hear that this game console is selling well due to its low price and user-friendliness.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S-plain という理由で "because" (lit. for the reason that~) is used to present the reason for a state, event, or action stated in the main clause. The phrase is usually used in written language.
この サイトは とても 役[やく]に 立[た]つけれど、 セキュリティに 関[かん]しては 問題[もんだい]が 多[おお]い。
This site is really useful, but it has a lot of security issues.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N に関して は S formal "with regard to; concerning; regarding; about; on; related to" について is similar in meaning to に関して, but is less formal and is used in both written and spoken language.
ルームメートは また 食[た]べた 皿[さら]を 出[だ]しっぱなしの まま 学校[がっこう]に 行[い]ってしまった。
My roommate left for school again without cleaning up his dishes.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-masu っぱなしの N "keep V-ing; leave" This is used when someone or something keeps doing X or someone did X but did not finish the action properly. As in this case, Vっぱなし is often used to describe an undesirable situation, but this is not always the case. Not used in formal language.
先週[せんしゅう]、 一[いち]年[ねん]生[せい]に 成[な]ったばかりの 学生[がくせい]の ための オリエンテーションが あった。
Last week, there was an orientation for students just starting their first year.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.past ばかり indicates that someone has just done something or something has just happened. The noun modification form is ばかりの. --- 英訳 [English translation]: have just V-ed --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.past ばかりだ V-plain.past ばかりの N
日本[にほん]に 行[い]ったら 英語[えいご]は 使[つか]わないで なるべく 日本[にほん]語[ご]だけで 生活[せいかつ] する つもりだ。
When I get to Japan, I'm going to try not to use English and to get by the best I can with just Japanese.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N だけで "just N (is fine/enough/etc.) N/Vだけで is used to express the idea that X or just doing X is fine or good enough or that one can do something just with X or by doing X.
友達[ともだち]を 空港[くうこう]まで 送[おく]ったげなきゃいけないから、 明日[あした]は、 早[はや]く 起[お]きなくちゃ。
I've gotta take a friend to the airport as a favor, so I need to get up early tomorrow.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
In casual conversation contracted forms are commonly used.
外国[がいこく] 語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう] すると いう ことは、 他[た]の 国[くに]の 文化[ぶんか]を 勉強[べんきょう] すると いう 事[こと]なのだ。
To learn a foreign language is to learn another country's culture.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to indicate what X is or what X means. なのだ makes the statement more emphatic. To make this expression more formal, use である in place of だ. --- 英訳 [English translation]: X is Y; X means that Y --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ XはY(という)ことなの{である/だ} : 日本人のことなのである。
この クラスは 毎月[まいつき] 試験[しけん]が ある 上[うえ]に 宿題[しゅくだい]も たくさん あるから、 とても 大変[たいへん]だ。
In addition to having a test every month, there's also a lot of homework for this class, so it's really tough.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S 上に "in addition to~; besides~; not only~but also~; moreover~; ~ as well" The conjunction 上に introduces additional information emphatically.
この 辞書[じしょ]は 大学[だいがく]の 本屋[ほんや]で 買[か]えます。 また、 図書[としょ]館[かん]で 借[か]りる ことも 出来[でき]ます。
You can buy this dictionary at the university bookstore. You can also borrow it from the library.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: In addition to the meaning "again," また expresses the meaning "also" or "additionally." --- 英訳 [English translation]: also; as well; additionally; in addition; moreover --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ また、S。
あの クラスは、 毎日[まいにち] 宿題[しゅくだい]や 小[しょう]テストが あるので、 大変[たいへん]なのでは ないだろうか。
That class has homework and quizzes every day, so I think it may be difficult.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This ending indicates the speaker's conjecture and is used to express an opinion in an indecisive fashion. Although the negative form ではない is used, there is no negative meaning. のではない{だろう/でしょう}か are used only in written language, and のではないだろうか is the more formal form. ん{ではないでしょうか/じゃないかな} are used only in spoken language. んじゃないかな is more casual. --- 英訳 [English translation]: I think that ~; Isn't it that~? --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Sのではないでしょうか。
道子[みちこ]さんは ちょっと 冷[つめ]た そうに 見[み]えるけど、 本当[ほんとう]は とても やさしい 人[ひと]らしい。
Michiko seems a bit aloof, but I heard that she's actually quite a kind person.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
〜らしい。 means: Seem; apparently; I heard that~; it looks like Nによると。 Means: according to N
日本[にほん]語[ご]の 「いただきます」や 「 ごちそうさま」に 当[あ]たる 言葉[ことば]は 英語[えいご]には ない。
There are no words in English that correspond to the Japanese itadakimasu and gochisousama.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

XはYに当たる。 X&Y = Nouns Means: X corresponds to Y; X is equivalent to Y; X is equal to Y This grammar is often used to contrast words/phrases in two languages or organizations/professional titles in two countries.
この 町[まち]は 車[くるま]が ないと 生活[せいかつ]が できないから、 どの 家[いえ]でも 一[いち]台[だい]か 二[に]台[だい]は 車[くるま]が ある。
You can't live without a car in this town, so every house has at least one or two.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When the particle は follows a quantifier (i.e., a word such as 3本 or 少し), it adds the meaning "at least." だけは and ぐらいは (or くらいは) after a noun have the same meaning. --- 英訳 [English translation]: at least. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Number (+ Counter) は b. N だけは c. N {ぐらい/くらい}は
トマトは 美味[おい]しいし、 いろいろな 料理[りょうり]に 使[つか]える。 また、 体[からだ]にも いい 食[た]べ物[もの]だ。
Tomatoes are delicious and can be used in lots of different dishes. What's more, they're good for you, too.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: In addition to the meaning "again," また expresses the meaning "also" or "additionally." --- 英訳 [English translation]: also; as well; additionally; in addition; moreover --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ また、S。
「生[せい]」や 「日[にち]」などの 漢字[かんじ]は、 読[よ]み方[かた]が たくさん あって、 覚[おぼ]えるのが 大変[たいへん]だ。
Kanji like 生 and 日 have a lot of different readings and it's hard to memorize (all of them).
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: など indicates that the given list is not exhaustive. When more than one item is listed, や is commonly used to connect the item. --- 英訳 [English translation]: N1やN2など = N1, N2 and others. N1やN2などのN3 = N3 such as N1 and N2; N3 like N1 and N2. N1やN2など、N3 = N3 such as N1 and N2; N3 like N1 and N2. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N1やN2など({は / も / が / を / に / の / etc.)} (N1 and N2 can be words or phrases).
日本[にほん]語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう] している 学生[がくせい]が、 自分[じぶん]達[たち]で 日本[にほん]語[ご]の ブログ サイトを 立[た]ち上[あ]げた。
Students studying Japanese started up a Japanese blog site on their own.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

立ち上げる （V-masu 上げる） transitive "to start (something); to start up; to boot (a computer)" Affixed to the masu-stems of verbs, 上げる forms compound verbs, adding meanings such as "finish something up," "upward" or "to a great extent." the meaning is determined by the preceding verb.
一[いっ]週間[しゅうかん]の 旅行[りょこう]の うち、 三[みっ]日間[かかん]は 東京[とうきょう]に、 後（の）[ご] 四[よん]日間[かかん]は 京都[きょうと]に 行[い]く 予定[よてい]だ。
Of the week of travel, I'm planning to spend 3 days in Tokyo and the remaining 4 days in Kyoto.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

後（の）Number (+ counter) "the remaining ~; the remainder of ~; the rest of ~" This use of 後 should be distinguished from 後 in the following example, where 後 means "~more." In this use, の cannot occur after 後. このプロジェクトには後三人必要だ。
その 人[ひと]の ことを 全[まった]く 知[し]らないと いう わけでは ないが、 あまり 話[はな]した ことは ない。
It's not that I have no idea who that person is, but we haven't talked much.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

まったく〜（という）わけではない "It's not that ~ totally/completely/extremely/etc." used for emphasis in affirmative sentences. often used to express the speaker's emotion. In negative sentences, it indicates complete negation. It is used with verbs (often in potential form) and i-adjectives in negative sentences. まったく〜（という）わけではない indicates partial negation.
今日[きょう]の 試験[しけん]は 決[けっ]して やさしくありませんでしたが、 みんな よく できていました。
The test today was by no means easy, but everyone did very well.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
決して A-nai {ない／なっかた／ありません／ありませんでした} This grammar expresses strong negation of an idea, situation, possibility, etc. or strong prohibition.
この 日本[にほん]語[ご] 練習[れんしゅう] サイトを 使[つか]うと、 文法[ぶんぽう]が もっと よく わかる ようになるでしょう。
If you use this Japanese practice site, you'll probably come to understand grammar much better.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ようになる indicates a gradual change over a certain period of time; it means that someone (or something) comes to the point where he/she does (or can do) something or does not (or cannot) do something. V-なくなる is synonymous with V-ないようになる. The difference is that the latter implies a more gradual change. --- 英訳 [English translation]: come to (be able to) V; not V now; not V any more. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-pastようになる (V is often the potential form)
何[なに]か 言[い]いにくい ことが ある とき、 最後[さいご]まで 言[い]わないのは 日本[にほん]人[じん]らしい 話[はな]し方[かた]だ。
Not completing the sentence is a typical Japanese way of talking when there's something that is hard to say.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N らしい means that something/someone is representative of N. and XはNらしい conveys the idea that X has the positive characteristics of N. NOTE: らしい is an i-adjective so the noun-mod and adverbial forms are らしい and らしく respectively.
私[わたし]は この 教科[きょうか]書[しょ]が 大好[だいす]きだ。 何[なに]より、 単語[たんご]と 漢字[かんじ]が 覚[おぼ]えやすいと いうのが いい。
I love this textbook. More than anything else, the way it makes it easy to remember vocabulary and kanji is good.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
何より（も） "before everything; above all; first of all; more than anything else; the most ~"
会議[かいぎ]には 世界[せかい]中[じゅう]から 人々[ひとびと]が 集[あつ]まった。 一番[いちばん] 遠[とお]い ロシアからさえ 参加[さんか]者[しゃ]が あった。
This conference drew people from all over the world. There were even participants from Russia, which is the furthest from here.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N (prt) さえ Means: even さえ is an emphatic particle. In non-conditional clauses it means "even." When さえ is used, the particle が never occurs, を usually does not occur, へ and the directional に are optional, and the other particles, including the LOCATIONAL に, で、と and から are mandatory.
うちの チームは 今日[きょう]まで ずっと 勝[か]ちっぱなしだ。 今[こん]シーズンは 全然[ぜんぜん] 負[ま]けていない。
Our team has been on a winning streak right up to today. We haven't lost a game this season.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-masu っぱなしだ／で "keep V-ing; leave" This is used when someone or something keeps doing X or someone did X but did not finish the action properly. As in this case, Vっぱなし is often used to describe an undesirable situation, but this is not always the case. Not used in formal language.
運動[うんどう] すればするほど、 健康[けんこう]になれるし、 やせられるから、 運動[うんどう]は 一石[いっせき] 二鳥[にちょう]ですね。
The more you exercise, the healthier and slimmer you can become; exercise kills two birds with one stone, don't you think?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-cond {V/A}-plain ほど "the (more) ~, the (more) ~" This structure is used when the more something happens or is in some state, the more another thing happens or is in some state. (When V is a suru verb, the second VN is usually omitted, as is seen in this sentence)
ここには 各[かく]先生[せんせい]の メール アドレスと、 各[かく]セクションの 教室[きょうしつ]の 番号[ばんごう]が 書[か]いてあります
The e-mail address for each instructor and the classroom number for each section are written here.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
各 + N "each ~; various" A prefix which adds the meaning "each; various." When the referent of the noun after 各 is unknown, it means "various."
次[つぎ]の 試合[しあい]は、 強[つよ]い チーム同士[どうし]の 戦[たたか]いに なるから、 どちらが 勝[か]つか 全[まった]く 分[わ]からない。
The next match is between two strong teams, so I have no idea which will win.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N同士 {が／で／を} Indicates that Ns do something together, that Ns do something to/for/against each other, or that someone puts Ns together in some way.
海[うみ]に 行[い]きたい 人[ひと]も いれば、 山[やま]に 行[い]きたい 人[ひと]も いて、 旅行[りょこう]の 計画[けいかく]が 全然[ぜんぜん] 決[き]まらない。
Some people want to go to the beach and some want to go to the mountains, so it's been impossible to plan this trip.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 も V-cond, N2 も V "some do ~ and others do ~; do ~ and ~ among other things; sometimes ~ and sometimes ~; there are times when ~ and times when ~; ~ and also ~; ~ and ~ as well" This structure is used to present actions or states (usually 2) as examples of possible or past actions/states. In many cases the actions/states are contrastive ones.
悲[かな]しい ことに、 大学[だいがく]を 卒業[そつぎょう] してから、 大学[だいがく] 時代[じだい]の 友達[ともだち]と 会[あ]えなくなってしまった。
Sadly, since I graduated from college, I haven't been able to see my college friends.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

A.plain.non-past ことに “It is~ that~; I am/We are ~ that ~; To my ~" ことに is used to express the speaker's feeling or subjective judgment about what is said in the main clause. ことに can only be used with a limited set of words.
先生[せんせい]が おっしゃる ように、 言葉[ことば]は 毎日[まいにち] 勉強[べんきょう] しなければ 上手[じょうず]にならないと 思[おも]います。
As our teacher says, I don't think you can become skillful at a language unless you study every day.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように is used when (1) X resembles Y, (2) when X is as Y shows, says, explains, etc. or (3) when X does something as shown/said/explained, etc. in/by Y. --- 英訳 [English translation]: like; as; as if --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N のように V-plain ように
日本[にほん]では、 日本[にほん]語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう] する 他[た]に、 色々[いろいろ]な 所[ところ]に 旅行[りょこう]にも 行[い]きたいと 思[おも]っています。
In Japan, I'd like to travel to various places in addition to studying Japanese.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Nの他に(も) is an adverbial phrase meaning "in addition to N." Verbs, adjectives and demonstrative adjectives can also precede 他に(も) to mean "in addition to V-ing," "in addition to being Adj." or "in addition to this/that." ~他(に)は also means "in addition to." In some contexts, the phrase can mean "except for; other than" --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~他に(も) = in addition to ~; besides ~他(に)は(~ない) = (not ~) except for ~; (not~) other than ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~他に(も); ~他(に)は {この/その/あの}他に(も)
昨日[きのう]は とても 天気[てんき]が 悪[わる]くて、 寒[さむ]かった。 それで、 試合[しあい]を 見[み]に 来[き]た 人[ひと]が 少[すく]なかった。
It was cold yesterday and the weather was really bad. Because of that, not many people came to see the game.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: It is a sentence-initial conjunction. It precedes a fact, conclusion, decision, etc. S1 is the cause/reason for the information stated in S2. それで cannot be used when S2 is the speaker's judgement, request or command. In this situation, だから should be used. Note that だから can be used in situations where それで is used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: because of that; so; that's why; for that reason --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ S１。それで、S２。
田中[たなか] 先生[せんせい]の 研究[けんきゅう]室[しつ]には、 百[ひゃく]年[ねん] 以上[いじょう] 前[まえ]の 辞書[じしょ]も あれば、 最近[さいきん]の 映画[えいが]の DVDも ある。
In Professor Tanaka's office there are dictionaries from more than a hundred years ago as well as DVDs of recent films.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1も V-conditional, N2 も V。 Means: some do ~ and others do ~; do ~ and ~ among other things; sometimes ~ and sometimes ~; there are times when ~ and times when ~; ~ and also ~; ~ and ~ as well. This sentence structure is used to present some members in a group, things in a category, actions someone takes, characteristics of something/someone, etc. among others. Although the form of the verb here is conditional, the meaning is NOT conditional in its usage.
A: どうぞ よろしく お願[ねが]いします。 B: こちらこそ、 どうぞ よろしく お願[ねが]いします。
A: I'm pleased to meet you. B: The pleasure is mine.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N こそ "the very ~; It is that~; in particular; precisely; definitely; only (when, by doing, etc~)" こそ emphasizes the preceding word, phrase or clause. When こそ is used, the particles は、が and を drop.
書[か]いてある ことが 分[わ]かっても 分[わ]からなくても、 とにかく 最後[さいご]まで 読[よ]んでみましょう。
Whether or not you understand what's written, let's just try reading all the way to the end.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-te も V-nai なくても "Whether V or not"
今[いま]の うちに 勉強[べんきょう] しておかないと、 後[あと]で 卒業[そつぎょう] できないと いう ことに なるかも しれない。
If I don't study now, while I can, I may end up unable to graduate later on.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S(という)ことになる Means: end up (with); mean that ~; cause This grammar is usually preceded by 1 of 3 types of sentences, here is is (3) a conditional clause, and indicates that the (non-) action, even or situation stated in the preceding phrase/clause leads to a logical conclusion or a certain situation.
今日[きょう]は 試験[しけん]が 二[ふた]つも あったんです。 それで、 昨日[きのう]は コンサートに 行[い]けませんでした。
I had two whole tests today, so I couldn't go to the concert yesterday.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: It is a sentence-initial conjunction. It precedes a fact, conclusion, decision, etc. S1 is the cause/reason for the information stated in S2. それで cannot be used when S2 is the speaker's judgement, request or command. In this situation, だから should be used. Note that だから can be used in situations where それで is used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: because of that; so; that's why; for that reason --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ S１。それで、S２。
外国[がいこく]に 住[す]んでみて、 初[はじ]めて、 外国[がいこく] 語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう] する ことが いかに 大切[たいせつ]か、 よく 分[わ]かった。
When I actually tried living abroad, I realized for the first time just how important it is to study a foreign language.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
いかに〜か "how; how much; in what way" This structure occurs as an embedded interrogative sentence, where いかに means "how (much)" or "in what way". This structure is commonly used in written language.
外国[がいこく] 語[ご]が 上手[じょうず]になりたかったら、 あきらめないで 毎日[まいにち] 勉強[べんきょう] し続[つづ]ける ことが 大切[たいせつ]です。
If you want to become skilled at a foreign language, it is important not to give up and to continue studying every day.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V−masu 続く Means: continue to; continue V-ing; go on V-ing; keep (on) V-ing;all the way; all the time This phrase is used when the subject continues doing something volitionally.
ある 日[ひ]、 うさぎと かめが 競走[きょうそう]を しました。 さて、 どちらが レースに 勝[か]ったでしょうか。
One day, a rabbit and a turtle raced. Well now, which one won the race do you suppose?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

(S1.) さて、S2. "well; now; well now" さて always occurs at the beginning of a sentence and signals that (a) the speaker/writer is beginning a new topic (the new topic and the previous topic may be part of the same discourse) (b) the speaker/writer is going to ask a question about the information just provided, AS SEEN HERE or (c) the speaker is leaving. さてis not used in casual situations.
歌[うた]の 次[つぎ]に ダンスが 始[はじ]まりました。 すると、 ますます たくさんの 人[ひと]が 集[あつ]まってきました。
After the singing ended, the dancing began, and more and more people gathered around.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ますます Adv "more and more; -er and -er; increasingly; even more; even -er; still more; still -er" ますます occurs with verbs, the adverbial forms of adjectives and adverbs. It indicates that something happens to an even greater (or lesser) degree than before. ますます is NOT used for future controllable events. For example, it cannot replace もっともっと in もっともっとがんばって下さい。
ここは セルフサービスですから、 それぞれ 自分[じぶん]の 好[す]きな 食[た]べ物[もの]を 取[と]って 食[た]べて下[くだ]さい。
Everyone, it's self-service here, so please each get the food you like and eat.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
それぞれ Predicate Means: each; one's own; in one's own way それぞれ is used to focus on each individual or thing in a group of people or things, and means "each (one of them)."
あの レストランは 静[しず]かだ。でも、 食[た]べ物[もの]が 美味[おい]しいのは この レストランの 方[ほう]だと 思[おも]う。
That restaurant is quiet. But I think it is this restaurant that has delicious food.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
説明 [explanation]: The structure SのはXの方だ is used to emphasize that it is X that makes the proposition in S true. --- 英訳 [English translation]: It is X that S --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ SのはXの方だ。
これらの 辞書[じしょ]の 中[なか]で、 もし どれか 一[ひと]つを 選[えら]ぶと したら、 やはり 電子[でんし] 辞書[じしょ]に するだろう。
If I were to pick one among these dictionaries, after all I'd probably decide on the elctronic one.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

（もし）S としたら Sとしたら literally means "If I/we/you suppose that S." This construction is usually used to present a hypothetical situation, but can be used for an actual situation as well in which the speaker is presenting the situation as if it were hypothetical in order to indicate something indirectly. もし here is optional. It emphasizes that the speaker is presenting the situation as a hypothetical one.
雨[あめ]の 場合[ばあい]は テニスの 試合[しあい]は ない。 その 場合[ばあい]、 チケットは 次[つぎ]の 試合[しあい]に 使[つか]う ことが 出来[でき]る。
In the event of rain, there will be no tennis match. In that case, you'll be able to use your tickets for the next match.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 場合 is a noun meaning "case, occasion, situation," but with a modifier it forms an adverbial phrase/clause meaning "when; if; in case." 時 can be used in place of 場合 as seen in this example: 分からない {時／場合} は、言って下さい。 However, 場合 cannot replace 時 when 時 refers to a specific time and does not mean "case; occasion; situation," as shown in the example below: 私が行った {時／ｘ場合}には、ミーティングが始まっていた。 --- 英訳 [English translation]: if; when; in case --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ DemA + 場合: {この/その/あの} 場合
私[わたし]の 大学[だいがく]の チームは 試合[しあい]に 出[で]る たびに、 負[ま]けてしまう。 もっと 強[つよ]くなってほしいなあ。
My university's team loses every match they have. I wish they'd get better.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past たびに "every time; each time; on every ~; whenever" たびに expresses the idea that each time someone does something, something else takes place. When たびに is modified by a noun, the noun refers to an action or certain time.
あの 図書[としょ]館[かん]は 日本[にほん]の 本[ほん]が 少[すく]なく、 日本[にほん]の 新聞[しんぶん]も 無[な]かったので、 一度[いちど]しか 行[い]かなかった。
That library didn't have many Japanese books, and it didn't have any Japanese newspaper either, so I only went there once.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The masu stem of a verb and the stem of an i-adjective + く indicate that the sentence is continuing. That is, they function like the English sentence connector "and." This use is generally restricted to written language. In spoken language the te-form of a verb or an i-adjective is commonly used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: and --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-masu、 ~ A-stem + く、 ~
この リゾートは きれいな 海[うみ]で 泳[およ]ぐ ことも できれば、 山[やま]に ハイキングに 行[い]く ことも できる。
At this resort you can swim in an unpolluted ocean as well as hike in the mountains.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1も V-conditional, N2 も V。 Means: some do ~ and others do ~; do ~ and ~ among other things; sometimes ~ and sometimes ~; there are times when ~ and times when ~; ~ and also ~; ~ and ~ as well. This sentence structure is used to present some members in a group, things in a category, actions someone takes, characteristics of something/someone, etc. among others. Although the form of the verb here is conditional, the meaning is NOT conditional in its usage.
作文[さくぶん]が うまく 書[か]けなくて、 書[か]いては 消[け]し、 消[け]しては 書[か]いていたら、 朝[あさ]に なってしまった。
I struggled with my composition, and while I was writing and deleting over and over again, morning came before I knew it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V1-te は V2 "V1 and V2 repeatedly/over and over again/many times/etc." The construction of VteはV is used when a set of actions is repeated over a period of time. It can be said once, or repeated, as here.
先生[せんせい]には、 「じゃあ、 また」では なくて、 「失礼[しつれい] します」と 言[い]わなくては いけませんよ。
You need to say "Shitsurei shimasu" to a teacher, not "Ja, mata".
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to indicate that a certain piece of information is wrong and, following that, to present the correct information. ではなく(て) is used in written language and じゃなく(て) is used in spoken language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: not A, but B --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N1 {では/じゃ}なく(て) N2 b. Phrase1 {では/じゃ}なく(て) Phrase2
健康[けんこう]の ためには、 肉[にく]でも、 野菜[やさい]でも、 なんでも バランス よく 食[た]べなくては いけませんよ。
To be healthy, you must eat in a balanced way, whether it's meat or vegetables or something else.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 でも N2 でも "including X and Y; whether (it is) X or Y" This is used to provide examples for the statement in the sentence. This structure implies that there are also things other than the examples which make the statement true. Note that XもYも (both X and Y) does not carry such an implication..
店[みせ]に 行[い]かなくても 買[か]い物[もの]が できると いう 点[てん]が、 ネット ショッピングに 人気[にんき]が ある 点[てん]です。
The fact that you can shop without going to the store is one of the factors contributing to online shopping's popularity.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
DemA点 "point; aspect; viewpoint; respect" 点 is used to mean "point" (in the sense of a single, fact, idea or opinion in an argument, discussion, etc.), "aspect," or "viewpoint/standpoint."
ビデオの 日本[にほん]語[ご]が 分[わ]からなかったので、 もう 一度[いちど]、 聞[き]き直[なお]したら、 今度[こんど]は よく わかった。
I didn't understand the Japanese in the video, so I listened to it over again, and this time I got it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-masu 直す "again, re-V" 直す, when attached to the masu-stems of verbs, creates compound verbs with the meaning "again; re-."
新[あたら]しい アルバイトは、 今[いま]までの 2[に]倍[ばい]、 すなわち、 1[いち]時間[じかん]当[あ]たり 3千[さんせん]円[えん]の 時給[じきゅう]が もらえる。
My new part-time job pays me twice what I've been getting up until now - that is to say, 3000 yen per hour.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
NP1/S1, すなわち NP2/S2 "that is; i.e.; namely" すなわち
コースを 開[ひら]く ためには、 学生[がくせい]が 五[ご]人[にん] 以上[いじょう] 必要[ひつよう]です。 それ 以下[いか]の 場合[ばあい]は、 キャンセルです。
In order to open the class there must be 5 students or more. In the event that it is less than that, the class will be canceled.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: X以上 and X以下 means "equal to or more than X" and "(equal to or) less than X," respectively. A Number + Counter or a demonstrative pronoun such as これ and それ commonly occurs before 以上 and 以下. When the topic is academic grades, grade symbols such as C and B can be used (e.g., C以上). --- 英訳 [English translation]: 以上 = or more 以下 = less than; or less --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Number (+ Counter) 以上/以下: ３年生以上 b. Demonstrative pronoun 以上/以下: これ以上; それ以下
東京[とうきょう]は 電車[でんしゃ]や 地下[ちか]鉄[てつ]や バスが 便利[べんり]な 街[まち]なので、 車[くるま]が なくても 生活[せいかつ] できると いう わけです。
Tokyo is a city where the trains, subways and buses are convenient. That's why you can get by even without a car.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
~わけだ。 is used in 3 situations. For this one it is (1) when a speaker provides the reason for a previous statement. Means: The reason is that ~; It means that ~; That's why~; No wonder~; naturally
文法[ぶんぽう]の 説明[せつめい]を 読[よ]んでも 分[わ]からない 事[こと]が 有[あ]る。 そんな 時[とき]は 先生[せんせい]に 聞[き]きに 行[い]く 事[こと]に している。
There are times when I can't understand the grammar even when I read the explanation. When that happens, I make it a habit to go ask my teacher.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain-nonpast ことがある is used when something occurs (or someone does something) occasionally. も implies that something else may also occur. Note: This phrase should not be confused with V-plain-PAST ことがある (e.g. 日本に行ったことがある。) which states previous experience. --- 英訳 [English translation]: There are times when ~, sometimes --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain-nonpast こと{が / も}ある
先生[せんせい]の 説明[せつめい]を 聞[き]いて、 この 言葉[ことば]の 意味[いみ]は だいたい 分[わ]かったけれど、 まだ 上手[じょうず]に 使[つか]えない。
After listening to my teacher's explanation, I understood the meaning of this word more or less, but I still can't use it well.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
だいたいV "mostly V; nearly V; almost V" だいたい means "most, almost, nearly (all), approximate." The meaning changes depending on what it modifies.
家[いえ]に 帰[かえ]って、 まず 最初[さいしょ]に する ことは、 手[て]を 洗[あら]って うがい (gargle)を する ことです。
The first thing I do when I get home is wash my hands and gargle.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
説明 [explanation]: まず is an adverb meaning "first of all." --- 英訳 [English translation]: first of all; first; to begin with; before everything
日本[にほん]人[じん]は、 「サービスが 第[だい]一[いち]」と いう 考[かんが]え方[かた]を、 ビジネスの 様々[さまざま]な ところで 生[い]かしている。
The Japanese put the "service first" mindset to work in various aspects of business.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
生かす "make the most of; make the best use of; use effectively; maintain" 生かす means literally "to keep alive," but it is also used to mean "to make the most of one's ability, etc"
インターネットで 調[しら]べる ことに よって、 世界[せかい]中[じゅう]で 今[いま] 起[お]こっている ことを 知[し]る ことが 出来[でき]る。
By searching on the Internet, you can find out what is happening right now throughout the world.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
~ことによって によって indicates the cause, the means, or the agent in passive sentences. In this sentence it indicates MEANS. "because; because of; due to; by V-ing; by means of; via; through; by"
田中[たなか]さんも あの 映画[えいが]、 見[み]たんですか？ 私[わたし]も 先週[せんしゅう] 見[み]たんですよ。 とっても 良[よ]かったでしょう。
You saw that movie too, Tanaka? I saw it last week, too. Wasn't it great?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: でしょう and だろう with rising intonation are used to elicit the hearer's confirmation. でしょう is the polite version of だろう. In casual conversation, male speakers use だろう and female speakers use でしょう. In more casual situations, the final う tends to drop. Note: でしょう and だろう with falling intonation indicate conjecture. --- 英訳 [English translation]: tag question(e.g. isn't it?; wasn't it?; aren't they?; is he?; are they?) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~だろう, ~でしょう
夏休[なつやす]みに 大学[だいがく]の 夏[なつ]の コースを 取[と]った。 その 他[た]にも、 バイトを したり、 日本[にほん]に 行[い]ったり した。
Over summer break I took university summer school courses. In addition to that, I did stuff like work my part-time job and go to Japan.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Nの他に(も) is an adverbial phrase meaning "in addition to N." Verbs, adjectives and demonstrative adjectives can also precede 他に(も) to mean "in addition to V-ing," "in addition to being Adj." or "in addition to this/that." ~他(に)は also means "in addition to." In some contexts, the phrase can mean "except for; other than" --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~他に(も) = in addition to ~; besides ~他(に)は(~ない) = (not ~) except for ~; (not~) other than ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~他に(も); ~他(に)は {この/その/あの}他に(も)
私[わたし]は 日本[にほん] 文学[ぶんがく]を 研究[けんきゅう] したいと 思[おも]っている。だが、 両親[りょうしん]は 私[わたし]に 医者[いしゃ]に なってほしがっている。
I think I'd like to study Japanese literature. My parents, however, want me to become a doctor.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1. だが、S2. "but; however" だが is a disjunctive conjunction. S1 and S2 present contrastive statements or opposing ideas. Note: でも、けれど、けど are colloquial けれども、しかしながら、だが、and が are primarily used in written language. しかし can be used in both written and spoken language.
この 教科[きょうか]書[しょ]を 使[つか]う ようになって、 学生[がくせい]たちの 日本[にほん]語[ご]が どんどん 上達[じょうたつ] したと いうのは 事実[じじつ]だ。
It's a fact that once we started using this textbook, the students' Japanese improved rapidly.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S (という）のは事実だ。 "It is {true/a fact that} ~" Used when the speaker wants to claim that something is true or is a fact, or when he/she admits that something is true or a fact. The presence or absence of という does not change the meaning.
昔[むかし]は いいと されていた ことが、 今[いま]は よくないと されている ことが ある。 タバコは その 一[ひと]つだ。
There are things that used to be considered fine but now are considered bad. Tobacco is one of these.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S-plain とされている "it is thought/believed/considered that~; ~ is considered/believed to ~" This is used to introduce a commonly accepted idea or belief.
この アイコンを クリック して下[くだ]さい。 すると、 コンピュータの 画面[がめん]の 文字[もじ]が 大[おお]きくなります。
Please click this icon. That will make the letters on the screen become bigger.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S1. すると、S2. "then" すると connects two sentences S1 and S2 in three situations. In this particular case, it is (2) The action in S1 leads to the discovery of what is said in S2
この 本[ほん]を 読[よ]むと、 昔[むかし]の ギリシャにも 日本[にほん]の ように 色々[いろいろ]な 神[かみ]様[さま]が いたと いう ことが よく 分[わ]かる。
If you read this book, you will understand well that ancient Greece, like Japan, had various deities.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S-plain ということ(が、を、etc) General meaning: that; V-ing changes a sentence into a noun clause, but does not add any meaning. The noun clause can be marked by が、を, etc. This phrase is usually used in WRITTEN language.
夏休[なつやす]みに 一[いっ]か月[げつ] アルバイトを して 15万[いちごまん]円[えん] もらった。 一[いち]日[にち]当[あ]たり 5千[ごせん]円[えん] もらった ことに なる。
I worked a part-time job for a month over summer vacation and got 150,000 yen. That comes to 5,000 yen per day.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 当たり is used with ー (or 1) and a counter to mean "per." Sometimes numbers other than one are used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: per~; a ~; for a ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Number + Counter 当たり Number + Counter b. Number + Counter 当たりの N
私[わたし]が 住[す]んでいる アパートは、 周[まわ]りが 静[しず]かなだけでなく 安全[あんぜん]でも あるので、 学生[がくせい]に 人気[にんき]が ある。
The apartment I'm living in is in an area that's not just quiet; it's also safe, so it's popular among students.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N／ANa でもある "be also" X は Y でもある. OR X は Y でもあり、Z でもある。 Are used to introduce another property of X when X has more than one property.
戦争[せんそう]が 良[よ]くない ことは、 みんな 分[わ]かっている はずだ。 しかしながら、 未[いま]だに 戦争[せんそう]は 続[つづ]いている。
Everyone should know that war is not good. However, war still continues even now.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S1. しかしながら S2. "however, but" しかしながら is a disjunctive conjunction and appears only in sentence-initial position. It is a highly formal expression and is used typically in written language.
受験[じゅけん] 戦争[せんそう]と いうのは、 つまり、 いい 学校[がっこう]に 入[はい]る ために、 戦争[せんそう]の ように 勉強[べんきょう]で 競争[きょうそう] する ことです。
In other words, the term "entrance exam war" describes the war-like academic competition to get into a good school.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N/NP （というの）は、つまり〜{だ／（という）ことだ} "That is (to say); in other words; namely; (that) means; you mean ~?" つまりis used to rephrase or restate what has just been mentioned or stated.
日本[にほん]では 外国[がいこく]人[じん]だと いう 理由[りゆう]で、 アパートを 貸[か]してもらえない ことが あるらしい。 信[しん]じられない。
Apparently, there are cases in Japan where foreigners cannot rent an apartment because they're foreigners. It's unbelievable.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S-plain という理由で "because" (lit. for the reason that~) is used to present the reason for a state, event, or action stated in the main clause. The phrase is usually used in written language.
1[いち]年[ねん]生[せい]の 時[とき]は 漢字[かんじ]が なかなか 覚[おぼ]えられませんでしたが、 今[いま]は、 あまり 時間[じかん]を かけずに 覚[おぼ]えられます。
When I was a first-year student I had a hard time remembering kanji, but now I can memorize them without spending too much time.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

なかなか V-nai ない "not easily; not readily; difficult to~; slow to; to refuse to" なかなか with V-nai is usually used when something desirable doesn't happen easily or when something that is supposed to happen doesn't happen.
犬[いぬ]は 外[そと]で トイレを するから、 天気[てんき]が よくても よくなくても、 毎日[まいにち] 散歩[さんぽ]に 連[つ]れて行[い]かなくては いけない。
Dogs go to the toilet outside, so whether it's nice out or not you have to take them for a walk every day.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
A-te も A-nai なくても "whether A or not"
A) ねえ、 あの 人[ひと]、 どこかで 見[み]た こと ない？ B） そう 言[い]えば、 昔[むかし]、 どこかで 会[あ]った ことが ある ような 気[き]が する。
A) Hey, haven't you seen that person somewhere before? B) Now that you mention it, I get the feeling that I've met that person somewhere a long time ago.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
そう言えば Means: That reminds me; Now i remember; indeed This conjunctive phrase is used when the speaker is reminded of something by the hearer's remark or the speaker's own remark.
面白[おもしろ]さと いう 点[てん]から 考[かんが]えると、 この 小説[しょうせつ]は あまり 面白[おもしろ]くないが、でも、 歴史[れきし]的[てき]な ことが 分[わ]かるので 勉強[べんきょう]に なる。
From the standpoint of being interesting, this novel is not very interesting, but you can learn some things about history, so it is informative.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N という点から考えると "to view from the standpoint of ~; from the perspective of ~" used to indicate someone's view from the standpoint of X. Examples of X include business, environment, education, etc.
日本[にほん]では ケータイで メールを する 人[ひと]が 多[おお]い。 それに 対[たい]して、 アメリカでは コンピュータで メールを する 人[ひと]が 多[おお]い。
In Japan, people mostly send e-mail with their cell phones. In contrast, most people in the United States send e-mail by computer.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Nに対して "whereas; on the other hand; in contrast" に対して is used when contrasting two actions, states, situations, etc.
スーツケースを 持[も]って 空港[くうこう]まで 行[い]ったんだ。 ところが、 飛行[ひこう] 機[き]が キャンセルに なって行[い]けなくなっちゃったんだ。
I went to the airport, suitcase in hand, but my flight was cancelled and I ended up not being able to go.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ところが is a sentence initial conjunction used when something takes place which is unexpected from the preceding context. The sentence after ところが represents an event or action the speaker cannot control. --- 英訳 [English translation]: however; but; nevertheless --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ S１。ところが S２ where S1=what's expected; S2= what actually occurred.
ロンドンの 大英[だいえい] 博物[はくぶつ]館[かん] (The British Museum)には、 約[やく]700万[ななれいれいまん]点[てん]の コレクションが あると いう。
It's said that the British Museum in London has around seven million pieces in its collection.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S-plain という "It is said that ~; They say that ~" This structure indicate that the preceding information is not first hand. This is a polite form.
ベートーベンは 音楽[おんがく]家[か]に とって 最[もっと]も 大切[たいせつ]な 耳[みみ]が 聞[き]こえなくなってしまったのに、 あの 有名[ゆうめい]な 「 第[だい]九[きゅう] シンフォニー」を 作[つく]った。
Despite losing his hearing, which is the most important thing for a musician, Beethoven wrote his famous Ninth Symphony.

説明 [explanation]: Xにとって means "to X; for X" in a context where something (or someone) is important to X, or is necessary, useful, good, difficult, etc. for X. 〜くせに Means: Although~; in spite of the fact that~; and yet~ This conjunction is used when something commonly expected from information in the subordinate clause (i.e. the くせに phrase/clause) does not happen or is not the case. In most situations, くせに expresses the speaker's anger, frustration or disagreement. This emotion is not directed toward the speaker, but toward the hearer or 3rd person. When くせに is used, the subject of the main clause and that of the subordinate clause must be the same. If the subjects differ, you must use なのに、.

説明 [explanation]: って is a colloquial topic marker. It often appears in questions. In written language, は can be used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Speaking of ~, As for ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N って

説明 [explanation]: V-teくる and V-teいく indicate the temporal or spatial direction of an action from the speaker's viewpoint. V-teくる is used when an action appears to be directed toward the speaker, and V-teいく is used when it appears to be directed away from the speaker. V-teくる often indicates that an action or process began in the past and is continuing in the present, or that something has begun to take place. V-teいく, on the other hand, often expresses an action or state that will continue from the present into the future. In other uses, 来る and 行くfollowing V-te maintain their original meanings, i.e., "to come" and "to go." --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-teくる = have V-ed; begin to; become; grow V−teいく = go on V-ing; continue; become; grow --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te来る/行く

説明 [explanation]: V-volとした, the past form of V-volとする(to try to do ~), is used in situations when someone had made an attempt to do something but failed, where someone was going to do something but didn't, or where something happened when someone was going to do something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-volとした{が／けれど} = tried to ~, but; was going to ~, but V-volとしたら = when ~ was going to ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-volとした{が／けれど}: 行こうとした{が／けれど／ら}; 食べようとした{が／けれど／ら}
